Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the last session! The players are already out in the middle now. Saim Ayub and Shan Masood are the two openers for Pakistan. Kagiso Rabada has the new red cherry in his hand and is raring to go. Let's go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

We have seen some uneven bounce on this pitch already and some turn as well which is encouraging signs for South Africa as they have the upper hand here. Their fast bowlers will look to exploit the overcast conditions and make early inroads. Pakistan, after some sloppy fielding and inconsistent bowling, only have themselves to blame for conceding this big lead. Now, their batters need to come out in these testing conditions and bat their skins out to set up a good target for the hosts. Join us around 1.20 pm GMT to catch all the exciting action in the final session.

Pakistan started the session well with Naseem Shah getting rid of Kyle Verreynne and Marco Jansen quite early. However, they couldn't really build on that and allowed the hosts to put the pressure back on them. With the lead quickly evaporating, Khurram Shahzad struck at a crucial time removing the set Aiden Markram on 89. One would have thought that it was just a matter of time before they wrapped things up and kept the host's lead to a minimum. But that was not the case, as they not only failed to do that but also conceded a huge lead before Saim Ayub got the last wicket.

With that, TEA ON DAY 2 HAS BEEN CALLED! South Africa have batted brilliantly here and ended up taking a lead of 90 runs which could be significant on this wicket. First, it was the stylish knock of Aiden Markram filled with fluent strokes that got them into a solid position but unfortunately missed out on a ton. Then, the debutant, Corbin Bosch stole the show with a magnificent unbeaten 81 off 93 that has put the hosts in the driver's seat here.

OUT! CAUGHT! Pakistan finally ends the agony. Corbin Bosch exposes his non-striker for the first time and he falls immediately. Quicker, fuller, looped up, turns away after pitching. Dane Paterson looks to loft it over long off but ends up hitting it straight up in the air. Khurram Shahzad circles underneath it as the ball swerves on its way down. Shahzad somehow manages to grab it in between both his hands over his shoulders. South Africa have been bowled out for 301 with a first-innings lead of 90 runs.

Kyle Verreynne and Aiden Markram will resume batting for South Africa. Naseem Shah to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

David Bedingham came and made quick 30 runs in just 33 balls with five boundaries in no time but he got out just before Lunch much to the frustration of his partner, Aiden Markram as that stand was starting to look dangerous. Markram was then joined by Kyle Verreynne, and they both will look to extend South Africa’s dominance in the next session. Pakistan, on the other hand, needs quick wickets to claw their way back into the game. The post-Lunch session will be crucial for both teams. Will the hosts pile on the runs to solidify their advantage, or can the Men in Green stage a comeback with disciplined bowling? Stay tuned for what promises to be an exciting battle starting at 10.40 am GMT.

Pakistan’s morning didn’t go as planned. The bowlers toiled hard because they lacked consistency. Captain Shan Masood’s decision to delay bringing in Khurram Shahzad, who had picked up two wickets yesterday, proved questionable as the attack seemed to miss the spark he brought on Day 1. However, it may have been because he is carrying a minor niggle. Aamer Jamal and Naseem Shah picked up a wicket each in this session, but even they didn’t pose consistent threats.

Aiden Markram played a composed and elegant innings, bringing up his fifty and positioning himself for a well-deserved hundred. His solid technique and shot selection have kept Pakistan’s bowlers at bay. Temba Bavuma, meanwhile, looked comfortable at the crease, scoring 31 runs before falling to Aamer Jamal while trying to defend and that ended the partnership of 70 runs between both batters.

SESSION SUMMARY - 98 runs, 2 wickets, 24 overs! South Africa dominated the morning session, heading into Lunch at a commanding 180/5, putting themselves in a strong position in the match. They added 88 runs this morning at the cost of just two wickets, narrowing Pakistan’s first-innings lead to just 31 runs. Starting the day at 82/3, the hosts capitalized on the loose bowling from Pakistan to strengthen their grip on the game.

As the conditions are set to be overcast, the batters will have to adjust to the testing pitch while the bowlers will look for signs of deterioration to extract more swing and seam. SuperSport Park is known for producing exciting Test cricket, and Day 2 will certainly offer plenty of action as both teams battle for dominance. It’s shaping up to be an intriguing Test match, and we can’t wait to see what unfolds next!

Pakistan will be aiming to break the current partnership early and expose South Africa's middle order. Their bowlers made early inroads yesterday, with Shahzad and Abbas sharing the spoils. If they can continue applying pressure and exploit the conditions, they will fancy their chances of restricting South Africa to a modest total. From a Pakistan perspective, much depends on the performance of their bowlers, but the batting department, having faltered on Day 1, will need to step up if they are to set a competitive target. Kamran Ghulam’s fighting 54 was the highlight of their innings, but the lack of support meant they were dismissed for 211. Pakistan's bowling must be stern, or they will risk letting the Proteas take full control and gain a significant lead.

On Day 1, South Africa’s bowlers were dominant, skittling Pakistan out for 211 with Dane Paterson and debutant Corbin Bosch leading the charge, taking five and four wickets, respectively. However, their batting innings faced challenges, with Pakistan’s bowlers, particularly Khurram Shahzad and Mohammad Abbas, making crucial breakthroughs. South Africa ended the day with Aiden Markram unbeaten on 47 and Temba Bavuma on 4, still at the crease. On Day 2, South Africa will look to build a solid partnership between Markram and Bavuma, with Markram likely to play a key role in guiding the team to a strong position.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the first Test between South Africa and Pakistan at SuperSport Park, Centurion! After a gripping opening day, the match is delicately poised with both teams having their moments. South Africa finds themselves trailing by 129 runs with 82 for 3 on the board while Pakistan will hope for some quick wickets. With both teams eager to take control, expect another exciting day of Test cricket filled with tension and tactical battles.

They will look to keep reducing the margin while the visitors will need to make early inroads to make things exciting. Day 2 will begin at 8 am GMT but you can join us early for all the build-up. South Africa wasted no time, wrapping up Pakistan's innings in just three balls before taking the field in the last session. The reply started shakily as Khurram Shahzad struck early, removing Tony de Zorzi and Ryan Rickelton in quick succession. But Aiden Markram, having a good record at this venue, counterattacked with fluent strokes, finding support from Tristan Stubbs until he fell to a Mohammad Abbas delivery that stayed low. Markram remained unbeaten on 47, and along with Temba Bavuma dug in, steering South Africa to Stumps with composure after an action-packed day!

Mohammad Rizwan and Kamran Ghulam took the fight to the Proteas with a spirited 81-run stand, with Ghulam scoring a gutsy fifty before falling right on the hour, followed quickly by Rizwan. Just when South Africa seemed in control, Salman Agha and Aamer Jamal added a vital 47 runs, and the last-wicket pair's gritty effort pushed Pakistan past 200. Dane Paterson was sensational with a well-deserved fifer, while debutant Corbin Bosch grabbed four wickets. Despite an extended session, the Proteas were left frustrated by the visitors’ remarkable resilience.

After being asked to bat first, Pakistan’s openers, Saim Ayub and Shan Masood, showed grit in the first hour, surviving Kagiso Rabada's probing spell to reach 36/0. But debutant Corbin Bosch turned the tide with his very first delivery, sparking a dramatic collapse as Pakistan tumbled to 56/4, losing four wickets for just 20 runs. South Africa’s disciplined bowling, led by Bosch and Dane Paterson, left the visitors reeling, though Mohammad Rizwan and Kamran Ghulam fought back with some counterpunching strokes seeing the rest of the session out.

An exhilarating Day 1 of the Boxing Day Test comes to a close! 293 RUNS SCORED, 13 WICKETS FELL! South Africa holds a slight edge, but the game remains finely balanced. The Proteas made excellent use of the conditions with the ball, and Aiden Markram showcased his brilliance with the bat. Pakistan showed glimpses of individual brilliance but will need a more collective effort to truly challenge the hosts. We lost out on a few overs, which was disappointing and with rain forecasted for the next four days, time could play a big factor in this game. Hopefully, the rain stays away and we get to see both teams fight it out for a result with a WTC final spot up for grabs for the Proteas.

He bowls on hard length, just outside off, from around the wicket, jags back in. Ryan Rickelton is tentative there and pokes at it from the front foot. The ball takes the outside edge and flies behind barely reaching the keeper, but Mohammad Rizwan dives forward to gobble it up. The replays also confirm it is a clean catch. South Africa two down now!
